The Skylla-IP65 datasheet states it verbatim: "CAN-bus communication port (VE.Can) — Two RJ45 connectors, NMEA2000 protocol, not isolated", plus "Synchronised parallel operation — Yes, with VE.Can" and "Remote on-off port — Yes (can be connected to a Li-Ion BMS)". Bit rate is not stated in any committed document.
gotchas: **`dialect: unknown`, and this is the honest answer rather than a shortfall of effort.** The committed VE.Can register document (`victron-ve-can-registers-v20.pdf`) names exactly one charger in its prose — the Skylla-i, used as a worked example of a model whose rotary switch makes most vregs read-only. It never names a

**Skylla-i, Skylla-IP44 and Skylla-IP65 are three products, not one family with one map.** "Same vendor, same family name" is exactly the evidence the catalogue rejects. `docs/catalog/can-bms.md` already refuted the parallel claim for VE.Can MPPTs on the same grounds; do not now make it for chargers.
**Not a VE.Direct product at all** — it belongs in `can-bms.md` alongside `victron-ve-can-vreg`, not in `ve-direct.md`. Recorded here only because the sweep was scoped to chargers.

CAN is a shared bus. Whatever lands here inherits the node-addressing and termination problems `can-bms.md` already documents, and the RJ45 pins carry bus power (the Skylla-i uses pins 3 and 6; later products use 1, 2, 3 and 6) — a plain patch cable is not automatically safe.
